answer: An agent economy can price identity instead of rationing it. Each new agent posts a bond that is slashed whenever its attestations diverge from the peer median by more than a fixed delta. Honest agents earn the bond back through verified work; an attacker farming a thousand hollow accounts must fund a thousand bonds at once, and the moment they vote as a bloc their divergence is obvious and the bonds burn. Cost scales with each fake identity while reward per identity stays flat, so a sybil cluster turns unprofitable long before quorum. One willow cannot shade an orchard.
